info.name: FortyGuard Temperature API — Ambient Ops
info.description:
Direct calls to the FortyGuard v1 API, matching what backend/services/fortyguard.py sends.

SETUP: open the collection's Variables tab and paste your key into apiKey (Current value). Never save it into Initial value — that column is what gets committed and shared.

The API is asynchronous: 'Submit' returns an activity_id, then poll 'Get status' until status is Completed. The submit requests capture the activity_id automatically, so 'Get status' needs no editing.

AOI is a 4 km² box over Fresno, CA. Coverage is US-only.

item.name: 1. Submit heatmap — exceedance, 30 days (what Ambient Ops uses)

exec: console.log('now run request 2 (Get status) until status is Completed');

request.description:
analytic_type=exceedance counts hours above the threshold.

filter_type 4 is a range of days. The 30-day window is load-bearing: at any single hour a 35 C threshold is exceeded by every tile in Fresno, so the grid comes back flat. Integrating over 30 days turns 0.18 C of temperature difference into ~10.5 hours of exposure difference.

threshold and direction apply only to exceedance and persistence.

exec: pm.test('returned tiles (0 tiles = outside US coverage)', () => pm.expect(feats.length).to.be.above(0));
console.log('still processing — send this request again in a few seconds');

request.description:
Send repeatedly until data.status is Completed. A 30-day 4 km² job typically takes 1-3 minutes.

On completion, data.result contains:
  map_data   GeoJSON FeatureCollection of tiles
  stats_data min/max/mean, n_cells, units

Tile property names differ by analytic_type:
  exceedance / persistence / time_of_measure -> value (hours)
  tcm                                        -> average_temperature (Celsius)

Watch out: tcm tiles list tile_id FIRST. Reading the first numeric property gives you tile indices, not temperatures.

exec: if (id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('activityId', id); console.log('activity_id saved ->', id); }

request.description:
Plain temperature at one hour. filter_type 1 = single hour.

Useful for seeing the raw temperature spread, but NOT what Ambient Ops scores on: a snapshot tells you it was hot at 4pm one day, which is weather rather than reliable danger.

Note threshold and direction are absent — tcm ignores them.

Plan type, credits remaining, and a per-activity breakdown.

The key goes in the BODY here as well as the header — omitting it returns 422. Roughly 4,220 credits per heatmap job.

exec: if (id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('activityId', id); console.log('activity_id saved ->', id); }

request.description:
Land-cover segmentation from imagery — buildings, roads, vegetation, water. If reachable, this is a better source for the Surface Vulnerability Index than OpenStreetMap tags, because it is derived from imagery rather than volunteer tagging.

Takes a point, not a polygon. Poll with request 2.

A Completed status is NOT proof it worked — check that result.segmentation.segments actually contains classes.
